attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated as his view.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the statement: current AI does not firmly have any of the three capabilities. The 'firmly' qualifier is kept. It is a firm present-tense observation, not hedged.

contract.note: The plain reading, dependable command of each capability in demanding scientific work, is fair and ordinary. Requiring evidence on all three components fits the wording. The thresholds for 'firmly' and 'Nobel-calibre' are reader-supplied, so interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: The ZebraLogic v1 preprint (Feb 2025) shows accuracy falling as logic puzzles get harder, including for o1 and R1. Predates the post. Supports the logic component, but only on one benchmark type.
The CounterBench v1 preprint (Feb 2025) finds most LLMs near random on formal counterfactual reasoning. Supports the causal component, but only on the tested models and task.

FunSearch (Nature, 2023) found new cap-set constructions using an LLM plus an evaluator. This qualifies any claim of zero originality, but it is a single, narrow, evaluator-driven result and does not show dependable originality.

Google's own blog post on its AI co-scientist (Feb 2025) reports novel AML drug candidates validated in the lab, with experts guiding the work. Company self-report, not independent validation. It neither shows firm command nor establishes limits.

reviews.rationale: Pre-publication evaluations (e1, e2) support limits in logic and causal reasoning on specific benchmarks. The contract requires evidence on all three components, but nothing here shows limits on originality: e3 and e4 show isolated or guided novel results and settle nothing either way. Nothing shows firm command of any one capability, so the claim is not contradicted. The originality component stays unsettled, and the narrow benchmarks are not representative of all systems at publication.
